ampicillin.name: Ampicillin (IV)
ampicillin.loadingDose: No loading dose reduction in renal impairment. For severe sepsis/meningitis, administer standard initial full dose.
ampicillin.note: High sodium content (~3 mEq/g). Neurotoxic (seizures, encephalopathy) at high doses in severe renal failure. Meningitis requires aggressive dosing.

rrt.ihd: 1 - 2 g IV q12-24h; give dose immediately post-HD on dialysis days (moderately dialyzed ~40%).
2 g IV q12h post-HD; redose immediately after dialysis session.
rrt.crrt: 2 g IV q6-8h (high ultrafiltration rates remove drug efficiently).

ampicillin-sulbactam.name: Ampicillin-Sulbactam (IV)
ampicillin-sulbactam.loadingDose: In severe sepsis/Acinetobacter infection, administer initial unadjusted loading dose of 3 g IV.
ampicillin-sulbactam.note: Dose ratio 2:1 ampicillin:sulbactam. In severe Acinetobacter baumannii infections, high-dose sulbactam component (up to 6-9 g/day sulbactam) is required under ID supervision.

rrt.ihd: 1.5 - 3 g IV q24h; administer dose post-HD on dialysis days (ampicillin & sulbactam both cleared ~35-45% by HD).
rrt.crrt: 1.5 - 3 g IV q8-12h (or 3 g q8h for high-effluent CVVHDF/Acinetobacter).

penicillin-g.name: Penicillin G (IV)
penicillin-g.loadingDose: Administer full unadjusted initial dose (e.g. 4 million units IV) in acute bacteremia/meningitis.
penicillin-g.note: Significant neurotoxicity risk (hyperreflexia, myoclonus, seizures) when high doses accumulate in renal failure. Contains 1.7 mEq potassium per million units of potassium penicillin G.

rrt.ihd: 1 - 2 million units IV q8-12h; give dose immediately post-HD (dialyzable ~20-50%).
rrt.crrt: 2 million units IV q6h (CVVH / CVVHD / CVVHDF).

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 2 million units IV q8h (close neuro monitoring)

rrt.ihd: 2 million units IV q8-12h post-HD on dialysis days.

piperacillin-tazobactam.name: Piperacillin-Tazobactam (IV)
piperacillin-tazobactam.loadingDose: In severe sepsis/Pseudomonas, give full initial unadjusted loading dose of 4.5 g IV over 30 min before extending infusion.
piperacillin-tazobactam.note: Synergistic acute kidney injury risk when combined with Vancomycin. Extended infusion (over 3-4 hours) improves pharmacodynamic target attainment in Pseudomonas sepsis.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 4.5 g IV q6h (standard) or 3.375 g IV q6h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 20 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 2.25 g IV q6h or 3.375 g IV q8h

rrt.ihd: 2.25 g IV q8h; give supplemental 0.75 g post-HD on dialysis days (or 2.25 g IV q12h with full dose post-HD; cleared ~30-40%).
rrt.crrt: 3.375 g IV q6-8h (or 4.5 g IV q8h extended infusion over 4h for CVVHDF).

cefazolin.name: Cefazolin (IV)
cefazolin.loadingDose: Give full loading dose of 2 g IV regardless of renal function in acute MSSA sepsis/surgical prophylaxis.
cefazolin.note: Workhorse for MSSA bacteremia, endocarditis, and surgical prophylaxis. In endocarditis, use 2 g IV standard.

rrt.ihd: 1 - 2 g IV post-HD on dialysis days (dosed 3x/week post-dialysis, e.g. 2 g after session or 1 g q48h).

ceftriaxone.name: Ceftriaxone (IV)
ceftriaxone.standard_dose: 1 - 2 g IV q24h (2 g q12h in meningitis)
ceftriaxone.loadingDose: Standard dosing. No loading adjustment necessary.
ceftriaxone.note: Dual elimination (biliary ~40%, renal ~60%). NO renal dosage adjustment required regardless of CrCl or dialysis, except maximum 2 g/day in combined severe hepatic and renal failure.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 - 2 g IV q24h (2 g q12h for meningitis)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 - 2 g IV q24h (max 2 g/day; no adjustment)

rrt.ihd: 1 - 2 g IV q24h (not significantly dialyzed, clearance < 10%; no supplemental dose post-HD needed).
rrt.crrt: 1 - 2 g IV q24h (2 g q12h for severe CNS infections).

ceftazidime.name: Ceftazidime (IV)
ceftazidime.loadingDose: Administer 2 g IV loading dose in Pseudomonas sepsis before renal interval adjustment.
ceftazidime.note: Neurotoxic risk in severe renal insufficiency. Rapidly removed by hemodialysis.

rrt.ihd: 1 g IV loading dose, then 1 g IV post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzed ~50%).

cefepime.name: Cefepime (IV)
cefepime.loadingDose: Give full loading dose of 2 g IV in severe sepsis before transitioning to renal interval.
cefepime.note: HIGH NEUROTOXICITY RISK: Non-convulsive status epilepticus, encephalopathy, and myoclonus occur frequently if unadjusted in renal failure. Strict dose reduction mandatory.

rrt.ihd: 1 g IV on day 1, then 500 mg IV q24h with full dose administered immediately post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~65%).
1 g IV post-HD on dialysis days (or 1 g q24h post-dialysis).
rrt.crrt: 2 g IV q12h (or 2 g q8h for high-effluent CVVHDF).

cefoperazone-sulbactam.name: Cefoperazone-Sulbactam (IV)
cefoperazone-sulbactam.note: Cefoperazone eliminated predominantly via biliary excretion (75%); sulbactam is renally eliminated (75%). Adjust for the sulbactam component in renal failure. May prolong prothrombin time (PT/INR); consider vitamin K supplementation.

adjustments.label: CrCl 30 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1.5 - 3 g IV q12h (max 4 g/day cefoperazone component)

rrt.ihd: 1.5 g IV q24h post-HD on dialysis days (sulbactam cleared by HD; give dose after session).

meropenem.name: Meropenem (IV)
meropenem.loadingDose: Administer full initial loading dose (1 - 2 g IV over 30 min) in severe septic shock before interval titration.
meropenem.note: Workhorse carbapenem in ESBL and polymicrobial ICU sepsis. Extended infusion (over 3 hours) optimizes time above MIC (fT > MIC). Dialyzed efficiently by hemodialysis.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 g IV q8h (standard or 3h extended infusion)

rrt.ihd: 500 mg IV q24h; give dose immediately post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~50%).
rrt.crrt: 500 mg - 1 g IV q12h (or 1 g q8h extended infusion for high-effluent CVVHDF).

rrt.ihd: 1 g IV q24h post-HD on dialysis days.
rrt.crrt: 1 g IV q8h (extended 3h infusion) for CVVHDF; 1 g q12h for standard CVVH.

imipenem-cilastatin.name: Imipenem-Cilastatin (IV)
imipenem-cilastatin.loadingDose: Administer full unadjusted initial dose of 500 mg - 1 g IV in acute infection.
imipenem-cilastatin.note: HIGHEST SEIZURE RISK among carbapenems if unadjusted in renal failure or pre-existing CNS lesions. Meropenem is preferred if seizure risk exists.

rrt.ihd: 250 - 500 mg IV q12h; administer immediately post-HD on dialysis days (cleared ~50%).
500 mg IV q12h post-HD on dialysis days.

ertapenem.name: Ertapenem (IV)
ertapenem.note: Convenient once-daily dosing. Lacks activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter. High protein binding (~95%). Neurotoxicity/hallucinations reported in ESRD.

rrt.ihd: 500 mg IV q24h; if dose is given within 6h prior to HD, administer a 150 mg supplemental dose post-HD. Preferably give dose immediately after HD.

levofloxacin.name: Levofloxacin (IV/PO)
levofloxacin.loadingDose: Administer standard initial dose (500 - 750 mg) on Day 1; subsequent doses adjusted by renal function.
levofloxacin.note: Renally eliminated (~80% unchanged). High risk of QTc prolongation, tendon rupture, and CNS toxicity. In severe renal failure, initial 500-750 mg load is essential.

adjustments.label: CrCl 20 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 500 mg initial, then 250 mg q24h (or 750 mg q48h)

adjustments.label: CrCl 10 - 19 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 500 mg initial, then 250 mg q48h (or 750 mg initial then 500 mg q48h)

rrt.ihd: 500 mg initial load, then 250 mg PO/IV q48h post-HD on dialysis days (minimally dialyzed < 10%).
rrt.crrt: 500 mg initial load, then 250 - 500 mg IV q24h.

ciprofloxacin.name: Ciprofloxacin (IV/PO)
ciprofloxacin.standard_dose: 400 mg IV q8-12h or 500 - 750 mg PO q12h
ciprofloxacin.note: Both hepatic and renal elimination (~50% renal). Oral bioavailability 70%. QTc prolongation and tendonitis warnings apply.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 400 mg IV q8-12h or 500 - 750 mg PO q12h

adjustments.label: CrCl 30 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 400 mg IV q12h or 500 mg PO q12h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 30 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 200 - 400 mg IV q18-24h or 250 - 500 mg PO q24h

rrt.ihd: 250 - 500 mg PO q24h or 200 - 400 mg IV q24h; give dose post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~10%).

moxifloxacin.name: Moxifloxacin (IV/PO)
moxifloxacin.note: Predominantly hepatic metabolism and biliary excretion (~80%). NO renal dosage adjustment required for any degree of renal impairment or dialysis. Lacks urinary concentration (do NOT use for UTI).

rrt.ihd: 400 mg PO/IV q24h (not removed by HD; no supplemental dose needed).

gentamicin.name: Gentamicin (IV)
gentamicin.loadingDose: MANDATORY FULL LOADING DOSE: 5 - 7 mg/kg (extended interval) or 2 mg/kg (traditional) based on Dosing Weight (ABW in obesity). NEVER reduce loading dose for renal failure.
gentamicin.note: SEVERE NEPHROTOXICITY & OTOTOXICITY RISK. Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) mandatory. Avoid concurrent nephrotoxins. Measure random level at 6-14h post-dose (Hartford nomogram) or trough before redosing.

adjustments.label: CrCl 40 - 59 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 5 - 7 mg/kg IV q36h (or per Hartford nomogram)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 20 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Load 2 - 3 mg/kg, then redose strictly per random drug levels (target trough < 1 mcg/mL)

rrt.ihd: Load 2 mg/kg IV; maintenance 1 - 1.5 mg/kg IV post-HD on dialysis days; redose strictly guided by pre-HD serum concentrations (dialyzable ~50%).
rrt.crrt: 2 - 2.5 mg/kg IV q24-48h guided by continuous TDM.

adjustments.label: CrCl < 20 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Load 1.5 mg/kg, then redose only when level < 1 mcg/mL

rrt.ihd: 1 mg/kg IV post-HD on dialysis days; monitor trough levels before next dose.
rrt.crrt: 1 - 1.5 mg/kg IV q24-48h guided by TDM.

amikacin.name: Amikacin (IV)
amikacin.loadingDose: FULL LOADING DOSE MANDATORY: 15 mg/kg based on Dosing Weight (ABW in obesity) in acute sepsis. Never reduce loading dose.
amikacin.note: POTENT NEPHROTOXIC & OTOTOXIC AGENT. Therapeutic Drug Monitoring mandatory (target peak 20-30 mcg/mL, trough < 5 mcg/mL). Dosed on ABW if BMI >= 30.

adjustments.label: CrCl < 20 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Load 7.5 - 10 mg/kg, then redose strictly per serum levels (target trough < 5 mcg/mL)

rrt.ihd: 5 - 7.5 mg/kg IV post-HD on dialysis days; redose strictly based on pre-HD serum concentrations (dialyzed ~50%).
rrt.crrt: 7.5 - 10 mg/kg IV q24-48h guided by TDM.

vancomycin.name: Vancomycin (IV)
vancomycin.loadingDose: MANDATORY LOADING DOSE: 20 - 25 mg/kg (up to 30 mg/kg in critically ill, max 2 g initial infusion) based on ACTUAL BODY WEIGHT (TBW) regardless of renal clearance.
vancomycin.note: NEPHROTOXIC: Synergistic nephrotoxicity with piperacillin-tazobactam, aminoglycosides, and NSAIDs. AUC24/MIC target 400-600 mg*h/L (or trough 15-20 mcg/mL in severe sepsis). Dosed using ACTUAL weight for loading.

adjustments.label: CrCl 15 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 15 mg/kg IV q24-48h (check trough prior to next dose)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 15 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Load 20 - 25 mg/kg, then redose when serum level < 15 mcg/mL

rrt.ihd: Load 20 - 25 mg/kg, then 500 - 1000 mg (or 7.5 - 10 mg/kg) post-HD guided by pre-HD trough level (target 15-20 mcg/mL; dialyzed ~30% with high-flux filters).
rrt.crrt: 20 - 25 mg/kg loading dose, then 10 - 15 mg/kg IV q24-48h guided by continuous TDM.

daptomycin.name: Daptomycin (IV)
daptomycin.loadingDose: Standard loading with prescribed dose (6 - 10 mg/kg).
daptomycin.note: Inactivated by pulmonary surfactant (DO NOT USE FOR PNEUMONIA). Monitor Creatine Phosphokinase (CPK) weekly (risk of rhabdomyolysis / myopathy). Dosed on Actual Body Weight.

rrt.ihd: 4 - 6 mg/kg IV q48h; administer dose post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~15-20%).
6 - 8 mg/kg IV q48h post-HD on dialysis days.
8 - 10 mg/kg IV q48h post-HD on dialysis days.

linezolid.name: Linezolid (IV/PO)
linezolid.note: 100% oral bioavailability. Primarily non-renal metabolism (~65% hepatic/tissue). NO dosage adjustment required for renal impairment. Dialyzable ~30% during 3h HD session. Monitor complete blood count (CBC) weekly for myelosuppression/thrombocytopenia if used > 14 days.

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 600 mg PO/IV q12h (no adjustment; two metabolites accumulate but clinical significance unclear)

rrt.ihd: 600 mg PO/IV q12h; administer dose post-HD on dialysis days (cleared ~30% by hemodialysis).

metronidazole.name: Metronidazole (IV/PO)
metronidazole.loadingDose: Administer standard loading dose (1 g or 15 mg/kg) in severe anaerobic sepsis/amebic liver abscess.
metronidazole.note: High oral bioavailability (> 90%). Primarily hepatic metabolism (60-80%). In severe renal failure, metabolites accumulate; neurotoxicity (peripheral neuropathy, encephalopathy) may occur with prolonged courses.

rrt.ihd: 250 - 500 mg PO/IV q8-12h; give supplemental dose immediately post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~45%).
500 mg IV q12h post-HD on dialysis days.

cotrimoxazole.name: Cotrimoxazole / TMP-SMX (IV/PO)
cotrimoxazole.note: Dosed on Trimethoprim (TMP) component. High risk of severe hyperkalemia and pseudo-elevation of creatinine (TMP inhibits tubular secretion of creatinine without altering true GFR). Maintain vigorous hydration to prevent crystalluria.

Uncomplicated Cystitis.standard_dose: 1 DS tablet (160 mg TMP) PO q12h x 3 days

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 DS tablet (160 mg TMP) PO q12h

adjustments.label: CrCl 15 - 29 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 SS tablet (80 mg TMP) PO q12h or 1 DS q24h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 15 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Avoid / Not recommended; if essential: 1 SS tablet PO q24h

rrt.ihd: 1 SS tablet PO post-HD on dialysis days (TMP cleared ~40-50% by HD).
rrt.crrt: 1 SS tablet PO q12h or 1 DS tablet q24h.

SSTI (Skin/Soft Tissue).standard_dose: 1 - 2 DS tablets (160-320 mg TMP) PO q12h

adjustments.label: CrCl 15 - 29 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 DS tablet (160 mg TMP) PO q12-24h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 15 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1/2 DS tablet (80 mg TMP) PO q24h with close potassium monitoring

rrt.ihd: 1 DS tablet PO post-HD on dialysis days.
2 - 4 mg/kg (TMP) post-HD on dialysis days.
2.5 mg/kg (TMP) IV/PO post-HD on dialysis days.
2.5 - 5 mg/kg (TMP) IV post-HD on dialysis days.
5 - 7.5 mg/kg (TMP) IV post-HD on dialysis days; check serum levels if available.

clindamycin.name: Clindamycin (IV/PO)
clindamycin.standard_dose: 600 - 900 mg IV q8h or 300 - 450 mg PO q6-8h
clindamycin.note: Hepatic metabolism (> 90%). NO renal dosage adjustment required for any degree of renal failure or dialysis. Not removed by hemodialysis. High risk of Clostridioides difficile colitis.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 600 - 900 mg IV q8h or 300 - 450 mg PO q6-8h (no adjustment)

adjustments.label: CrCl 10 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 600 - 900 mg IV q8h or 300 - 450 mg PO q6-8h (no adjustment)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 600 - 900 mg IV q8h or 300 - 450 mg PO q6-8h (no adjustment)

rrt.ihd: 600 - 900 mg IV q8h (not removed by HD; no supplemental dose needed).

nitrofurantoin.name: Nitrofurantoin (PO)
nitrofurantoin.contraindication: CONTRAINDICATED in CrCl < 30 mL/min (and cautioned in CrCl 30-60 mL/min). Inadequate urinary drug concentrations result in therapeutic failure; toxic systemic accumulation causes peripheral polyneuropathy, pulmonary fibrosis, and hepatotoxicity.
nitrofurantoin.note: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION in CrCl < 30 mL/min. Indicated ONLY for uncomplicated lower cystitis (lacks tissue penetration; ineffective for pyelonephritis).

adjustments.label: CrCl 30 - 59 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 100 mg PO q12h (use with caution, avoid if CrCl < 45 or long duration)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 30 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED: Ineffective urinary concentration & toxic systemic accumulation causing peripheral neuropathy

rrt.ihd: CONTRAINDICATED in hemodialysis patients.
rrt.crrt: CONTRAINDICATED in CRRT patients (ineffective urinary concentration).

acyclovir-iv.name: Acyclovir (IV)
acyclovir-iv.loadingDose: Administer full initial loading dose in acute viral encephalitis/disseminated infection before adjusting interval.
acyclovir-iv.note: HIGH RISK OF CRYSTAL NEPHROPATHY & NEUROTOXICITY (tremors, hallucinations, delirium, coma). Maintain vigorous IV hydration and slow 1-hour infusion. Dosed on Dosing Weight (IBW or ABW in obesity).

Prophylaxis: BMT.standard_dose: 250 mg/m2 IV q8h or 5 mg/kg IV q8h

rrt.ihd: 2.5 mg/kg IV q24h; give dose immediately post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzed ~60%).
125 mg/m2 IV post-HD on dialysis days.
2.5 mg/kg IV q24h post-HD on dialysis days.
5 mg/kg IV q24h post-HD on dialysis days (redose after each HD session).

acyclovir-po.name: Acyclovir (Oral)
acyclovir-po.note: Low oral bioavailability (15-30%). Maintain adequate fluid intake to avoid renal crystalluria.

rrt.ihd: 800 mg PO q12h; give supplemental 800 mg dose post-HD on dialysis days.
200 - 400 mg PO q12h post-HD on dialysis days.

valacyclovir.name: Valacyclovir (PO)
valacyclovir.note: Prodrug with 55% oral bioavailability (3-5x higher serum levels than oral acyclovir). NEUROTOXICITY (hallucinations, confusion, coma) occurs readily in unadjusted renal impairment.

rrt.ihd: 500 mg PO q24h; give dose immediately post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzable ~33%).

Genital Herpes.standard_dose: 1 g PO q12h (initial) or 500 mg PO q12h (recurrent)

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 g PO q12h or 500 mg PO q12h

rrt.ihd: 500 mg PO q24h post-HD on dialysis days.

Herpes Labialis.standard_dose: 2 g PO q12h x 1 day (2 doses)

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 2 g PO q12h x 1 day (2 doses total)

adjustments.label: CrCl 30 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1 g PO q12h x 1 day (2 doses total)

adjustments.label: CrCl 10 - 29 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 500 mg PO q12h x 1 day (2 doses total)

rrt.ihd: 500 mg PO single dose post-HD.

valganciclovir.name: Valganciclovir (PO)
valganciclovir.note: Oral prodrug of ganciclovir (60% bioavailability). Severe bone marrow suppression (neutropenia, thrombocytopenia). STRICT RENAL DOSE TITRATION MANDATORY to prevent fatal cytopenias.

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Not recommended; use IV ganciclovir for precision

rrt.ihd: Not recommended (use IV ganciclovir for accurate dosing post-HD); if unavoidable: 450 mg PO twice weekly post-HD.
rrt.crrt: 450 mg PO q24h (consult infectious disease specialist).

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: Not recommended; switch to IV ganciclovir

rrt.ihd: Not recommended; switch to IV ganciclovir post-HD.
rrt.crrt: 450 mg PO q48h or twice weekly.

ganciclovir.name: Ganciclovir (IV)
ganciclovir.loadingDose: Administer standard initial dose before adjusting interval.
ganciclovir.note: Renally cleared (> 90%). Severe dose-dependent granulocytopenia and thrombocytopenia. Monitor absolute neutrophil count (ANC) and platelets at least twice weekly.

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 1.25 mg/kg IV 3 times per week after HD

rrt.ihd: 1.25 mg/kg IV administered post-HD on dialysis days (dialyzed ~50%).

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 0.625 mg/kg IV 3 times per week after HD

rrt.ihd: 0.625 mg/kg IV post-HD on dialysis days.

oseltamivir.name: Oseltamivir (PO)
oseltamivir.loadingDose: Administer standard initial 75 mg dose immediately upon presentation of severe influenza.
oseltamivir.note: Prodrug converted to active metabolite oseltamivir carboxylate, which is eliminated entirely by glomerular filtration and tubular secretion (> 99%). Well tolerated.

adjustments.label: CrCl 11 - 30 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 30 mg PO once daily (q24h) x 5 days

adjustments.label: CrCl ≤ 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 30 mg PO single dose (or 30 mg post-HD every other session)

rrt.ihd: 30 mg PO post every other HD session (after session 1 and 3 in a 3x/week HD regimen).

Prophylaxis.standard_dose: 75 mg PO once daily (q24h) x 10 days

adjustments.label: CrCl ≤ 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 30 mg PO post every other HD session

rrt.ihd: 30 mg PO post every other HD session on dialysis days.

fluconazole.name: Fluconazole (IV/PO)
fluconazole.loadingDose: FULL LOADING DOSE MANDATORY: 800 mg (or 12 mg/kg) on Day 1 in candidemia/severe sepsis. Renal adjustment applies strictly to Day 2 onward.
fluconazole.note: Renally cleared (~80% unchanged in urine). Oral and IV formulations are therapeutically bioequivalent (1:1 conversion). Always administer a 100% loading dose on Day 1.

Candidemia / Severe.standard_dose: 800 mg load, then 400 mg PO/IV q24h

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 800 mg load, then 400 mg PO/IV q24h (100% dose)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 800 mg load, then 200 mg PO/IV q24h (50% dose)

rrt.ihd: 800 mg load, then 200 mg q24h; give 100% supplemental dose (200-400 mg) post-HD on dialysis days (cleared ~50%).
rrt.crrt: 800 mg load, then 400 - 800 mg IV q24h (high clearance on CVVHDF).

adjustments.label: CrCl < 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 200 - 400 mg load, then 50 - 100 mg q24h (50% dose)

rrt.ihd: 100 - 200 mg post-HD on dialysis days.

C. glabrata (SDD).standard_dose: 800 mg load, then 800 mg PO/IV q24h

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 800 mg load, then 800 mg PO/IV q24h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 800 mg load, then 400 mg PO/IV q24h

rrt.ihd: 800 mg load, then 400 mg post-HD on dialysis days.

voriconazole.name: Voriconazole (IV/PO)
voriconazole.standard_dose: IV: 6 mg/kg q12h x 2 doses load, then 4 mg/kg q12h; PO: 200 mg q12h
voriconazole.loadingDose: Day 1 loading dose: IV 6 mg/kg q12h x 2 doses (or PO 400 mg q12h x 2 doses).
voriconazole.contraindication: INTRAVENOUS FORMULATION CAUTION: IV vehicle SBECD (sulfobutylether beta-cyclodextrin) accumulates in CrCl < 50 mL/min and may cause acute tubular necrosis. STRONGLY RECOMMEND SWITCHING TO ORAL VORICONAZOLE (100% bioavailable, no SBECD vehicle).
voriconazole.note: Extensively metabolized by hepatic CYP2C19. Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) recommended (target trough 1.5-5.0 mcg/mL). Visual disturbances and hallucinations reported.

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: IV: 6 mg/kg q12h load, then 4 mg/kg q12h; PO: 200 mg q12h

adjustments.label: CrCl < 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: SWITCH TO ORAL VORICONAZOLE: 200 mg PO q12h (avoids toxic SBECD vehicle accumulation)

rrt.ihd: 200 mg PO q12h (oral preferred; neither voriconazole nor SBECD is effectively dialyzed; no post-HD supplement needed).
rrt.crrt: 200 mg PO q12h (or IV with caution if enteral route unavailable).

posaconazole.name: Posaconazole (PO/IV)
posaconazole.standard_dose: Delayed-Release Tablets: 300 mg PO q12h Day 1, then 300 mg PO q24h
posaconazole.loadingDose: Day 1: 300 mg PO/IV q12h x 2 doses.
posaconazole.note: Delayed-release tablet formulation preferred. Primarily eliminated via hepatic glucuronidation and fecal excretion (~70%). No renal adjustment for oral formulation. IV form contains SBECD vehicle (avoid in CrCl < 50).

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 300 mg PO (delayed-release) q24h (after 300 mg q12h load Day 1)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 300 mg PO (delayed-release) q24h (oral preferred; avoid IV form due to SBECD accumulation)

rrt.ihd: 300 mg PO q24h (not removed by hemodialysis; no supplemental dose needed).

caspofungin.name: Caspofungin (IV)
caspofungin.standard_dose: 70 mg IV Day 1 load, then 50 mg IV q24h (70 mg if > 80 kg or moderate hepatic impairment)
caspofungin.loadingDose: 70 mg IV loading dose Day 1 mandatory.
caspofungin.note: Hepatic metabolism and spontaneous degradation. NO renal dosage adjustment required for any degree of renal failure or dialysis. Not dialyzable. Adjust only for moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B: 35 mg daily).

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 70 mg IV Day 1, then 50 mg IV q24h (no adjustment)

adjustments.label: CrCl 10 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 70 mg IV Day 1, then 50 mg IV q24h (no adjustment)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 10 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 70 mg IV Day 1, then 50 mg IV q24h (no adjustment)

rrt.ihd: 70 mg load, then 50 mg IV q24h (not dialyzed; no post-HD supplement needed).
rrt.crrt: 70 mg load, then 50 - 70 mg IV q24h.

micafungin.name: Micafungin (IV)
micafungin.standard_dose: 100 mg IV q24h (Candidemia) or 150 mg IV q24h (Esophageal Candidiasis)
micafungin.note: Eliminated via feces and bile through non-CYP hepatic metabolism. NO dosage adjustment required for any degree of renal impairment or dialysis. Highly protein bound (~99%).

adjustments.label: CrCl ≥ 50 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 100 mg IV q24h (150 mg for esophageal) (no adjustment)

rrt.ihd: 100 mg IV q24h (not removed by hemodialysis; no supplemental dose needed).

amphotericin-b.name: Amphotericin B - Liposomal (IV)
amphotericin-b.standard_dose: 3 - 5 mg/kg IV q24h (up to 10 mg/kg in mucormycosis)
amphotericin-b.note: POTENT NEPHROTOXIC AGENT (vasoconstriction of afferent arterioles & distal tubular damage). Liposomal formulation significantly reduces but does not eliminate nephrotoxicity compared to deoxycholate. Pre-hydrate with 500-1000 mL normal saline prior to infusion. Monitor potassium and magnesium daily.

adjustments.label: CrCl 20 - 49 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 3 - 5 mg/kg IV q24h (monitor renal labs and electrolytes closely)

adjustments.label: CrCl < 20 mL/min
adjustments.recommendation: 3 - 5 mg/kg IV q24h (minimal renal elimination; monitor for progressive AKI)

rrt.ihd: 3 - 5 mg/kg IV q24h post-HD on dialysis days (negligible clearance by HD; no supplement needed).
